info.title: Navixy Platform API
info.summary: API calls for end-user applications built on the Navixy platform
info.description:
This is an API reference for the Navixy Platform API, the backend used by end-user applications.

**Coverage.** This specification is being adopted resource family by resource family. It currently covers the `user` family, meaning authentication, sessions, settings, personal information, audit records and applications; fleet vehicles and their service works; billing, meaning bills, payment systems, subscriptions, plans and transactions; the driver journal; depots; and field service tasks, meaning tasks, checkpoints, task history and task forms; and task routes, route optimization and recurring task schedules; and points of interest, POI import, forms and form templates; and employees, departments and check-ins; and sub-users, security groups and platform plugins; and API keys, spreadsheet imports, files, notifications, timezones and the events history; and reports, report schedules, tags and customizable entities; and geofences, geofence import, asset tracks and asset groups; and the tracking services, meaning APN lookup, BLE beacon data, delivery tracking, geocoding, map layers and data forwarding; and working statuses; and geo links, working status lists, routing and tracks.

**Parameters.** All parameters are documented in the JSON request body. The API also accepts them as form-encoded body fields or query-string parameters. See the authentication page for the general rule.

**Errors.** An error is signalled by a non-200 HTTP status, with an API-level code in `status.code` of the response body. The default status is 400. Validation failures add an `errors` array naming each offending parameter. Per-operation error code lists are documented on the prose pages next to each operation.

**Credentials.** Most operations accept either a user session hash or an API key in the `Authorization` header. A few accept a session hash only, and reject an API key with error code 4; those are called out in the operation description.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Operations for authenticating a user, managing their sessions, reading and updating their settings and personal information, reading audit records, and registering custom applications. All resources under the /user/ path.

tags.name: Vehicles
tags.description: Vehicles in the fleet, their avatars and status list, spreadsheet import, and the service works scheduled against them. All resources under the /vehicle/ path.

tags.name: Billing
tags.description: Bills, payment systems, subscriptions, device plans and the transaction log. All resources under the /bill/, /payment_system/, /subscription/, /tariff/ and /transaction/ paths.

tags.name: Driver journal
tags.description: Trips categorised as work, personal or other, and the proposals a track can be turned into. All resources under the /driver/journal/ path.

tags.name: Garages
tags.description: Depots where vehicles are kept and maintained. All resources under the /garage/ path.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Field service tasks: the places to visit, the routes and checkpoints they group into, the history of every change, and the forms field employees fill in. All resources under the /task/ path.

tags.name: Places
tags.description: Points of interest: the business-specific places employees visit, their avatars, spreadsheet import and bulk upload. All resources under the /place/ path.

tags.name: Forms
tags.description: Forms and the templates they are issued from. All resources under the /form/ path. Forms attached to tasks are under /task/form/ and carry the Tasks tag.

tags.name: Employees
tags.description: Employees and drivers, their avatars, spreadsheet import, and the departments they belong to. All resources under the /employee/ and /department/ paths.

tags.name: Check-ins
tags.description: Check-ins recorded by field employees from the Mobile Tracker App, with their photos and forms. All resources under the /checkin/ path.

tags.name: Sub-users
tags.description: Additional users under a master account: their security groups, and the trackers, places and geofences each one can see. All resources under the /subuser/ path.

tags.name: Account and platform
tags.description: Platform-level resources shared across the account, such as the plugins that change how other calls behave.

tags.name: History
tags.description: The events history: what happened on trackers and assets, what the account itself did, and which entries the user has read. All resources under the /history/ path.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Generating tracker reports, fetching them as JSON or as files, and scheduling them to be emailed regularly. All resources under the /report/ path.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: Labels applied across places, tasks, employees, vehicles, geofences and trackers, and the search that finds records by them. All resources under the /tag/ path.

tags.name: Entities
tags.description: Customizable record classes and the custom fields added to them. All resources under the /entity/ path.

tags.name: Geofences
tags.description: Geofences of all three shapes, their points, and spreadsheet and KML import and export. All resources under the /zone/ path.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: Tracks belonging to an asset rather than to a tracker, and the groups assets are organised into. All resources under the /asset/track/ and /asset_group/ paths.

tags.name: Tracking services
tags.description: Services supporting tracking rather than the trackers themselves: APN lookup, BLE beacon data, delivery tracking, geocoding, map layers and data forwarding. Resources under the /apn_settings/, /beacon/, /delivery/, /geocoder/, /map_layer/ and /retranslator/ paths.

tags.name: Working statuses
tags.description: Working statuses, the activity a tracker is marked as being in, the lists they are grouped into, and the assignment of a status to a tracker. All resources under the /status/ path.

tags.name: Trackers
tags.description: Trackers, the devices the platform tracks, together with the geo links that share their live location with people outside the account. Resources under the /tracker/ path.

tags.name: Routes
tags.description: Routing between points, using the account's default provider or a named one. All resources under the /route/ path.

tags.name: Tracks
tags.description: The trips a tracker made, the points behind them, the geofences and places they passed through, and waybills built from them. All resources under the /track/ path.

post.description:
Exchange a login and password for a session hash. Requires no credential of its own, and accepts no existing session.

The returned hash is what the `Authorization: NVX <hash>` header carries on subsequent calls. An API key may be used instead of a session hash on most operations, but a small number accept a session hash only. See the operation descriptions.

login.description: User email as login, or a demo login.

dealer_id.description: Optional. If specified, the API checks that the user belongs to this dealer and returns error 102 if not.

200.description: A new session, or a challenge when a second factor is required

type.description: Which outcome this is. `authenticated` means the session is ready to use. `second_factor_required` means multi-factor authentication is enabled and the returned hash is an MFA session, usable only for the `user/auth/code/*` operations until a code is verified.

factor_type.description: Which second factor is in use. Present only when `type` is `second_factor_required`. Only `email` is available at the moment.

hash.description: Session hash to send in the `Authorization` header. When `type` is `second_factor_required` it is an MFA session and is accepted only by the `user/auth/code/*` operations.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Access denied, error code 11, when the dealer is blocked. Error codes 102 wrong login or password, 103 user not activated, 104 logins limit exceeded, and 105 login attempts limit exceeded return the default 400.

post.description:
Complete a multi-factor authentication challenge by submitting the code that was sent to the user.

**Requires an MFA session**, which is issued part-way through authentication. An ordinary session hash or API key cannot call this operation.

code.description: The verification code sent to the user.

hash.description: Session hash for the authenticated session.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Send the multi-factor authentication code again.

**Rate limited to one call every 5 minutes** to prevent abuse.

**Requires an MFA session**, which is issued part-way through authentication. An ordinary session hash or API key cannot call this operation.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Activate the current user account.

**Requires an activation session**, so an ordinary session hash or API key cannot call this operation. Also requires the `admin` right.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right.

post.description:
Return the current user, the platform settings that apply to them, their tariff restrictions, granted rights, enabled features, and menu.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

application.description: Optional. If specified, the response includes a description of that application's custom menu.

paas_id.description: Identifier of the platform the user belongs to.

privileges.description: Rights granted to the current user.

rights.description: Sub-user right names held by the caller.

features.description: Names of features enabled for the user.

menu.description: Deprecated menu structure. Null on current platforms.

premium_gis.description: Whether the premium GIS package is active.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return the restrictions the user's tariff imposes.

**Requires a weblocator session.** Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Send the account activation email again.

Requires no credential. A session may be supplied and is used if valid, but is not required.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Error code 265 already done, when the account is already activated and verified. Error code 264 timeout not reached, when the previous activation link was generated less than 5 minutes ago, or another server-configured timeout. The 264 body adds `timeout` and `remainder`, both ISO 8601 durations, giving the configured interval and the time left before the next attempt.

post.description:
End the current session.

**Requires a session hash. An API key is rejected** with error code 4, "User or API key not found or session ended", which is misleading: the key is valid, but this operation accepts standard sessions only.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Replace the user's personal and address information.

**Requires the platform plugin with id 45.** Without it the call fails with error code 222, plugin not found.

**This is a full replacement, not a merge.** Fields omitted from the request are cleared.

`phone` is required and must not be empty.

phone.description: Contact phone, up to 15 digits. Required and must not be empty.

post_country.description: Optional. Country part of the user's post address.

post_index.description: Optional. Index part of the user's post address.

post_region.description: Optional. Region part of the user's post address.

post_city.description: Optional. City part of the user's post address.

post_street_address.description: Optional. Street part of the user's post address.

iec.description: Industrial Enterprises Classifier, also known as KPP. Used in Russia. For `legal_entity` only.

okpo_code.description: Optional. All-Russian Classifier of Enterprises and Organizations, 8 or 10 characters.

state_reg_num.description: Optional. State registration number, up to 15 characters. For example EIN in the USA or OGRN in Russia.

registered_country.description: Country part of the user's registered address.

registered_index.description: Index part of the user's registered address.

registered_region.description: Region part of the user's registered address.

registered_city.description: City part of the user's registered address.

registered_street_address.description: Street part of the user's registered address.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return the current user's settings.

`file_storage_settings`, `balance_alert_settings`, `first_user_balance_warning_period`, and `second_user_balance_warning_period` are **absent entirely** unless the caller holds the `admin` right, rather than merely read-only.

The `settings` object is filtered by the dealer's GIS package before being returned, so some fields may be absent or null on platforms with a restricted package.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

file_storage_settings.description: Present only when the caller holds the `admin` right.

balance_alert_settings.description: Present only when the caller holds the `admin` right.

first_user_balance_warning_period.description: How long before a projected zero balance the first alert is sent, as a duration such as `8d`. Present only when the caller holds the `admin` right.

second_user_balance_warning_period.description: How long before a projected zero balance the second alert is sent, as a duration such as `2d`. Present only when the caller holds the `admin` right.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Replace the current user's settings.

**This is a full replacement, not a merge, and only `time_zone` is required.** Any writable field omitted from the request is cleared, including `date_format` and `hour_mode`.

Send every field you intend to keep. `file_storage_settings` and `balance_alert_settings` are stored separately and do survive omission.

Updating `balance_alert_settings` or `file_storage_settings` requires the `admin` right.

date_format.description: Date representation. **Cleared if omitted**, and absent from the parameter list on older prose pages, which is how it gets wiped unnoticed.

hour_mode.description: Time representation. **Cleared if omitted**, and absent from the parameter list on older prose pages, which is how it gets wiped unnoticed.

translit.description: `true` if SMS notifications should be transliterated.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right needed for `balance_alert_settings` or `file_storage_settings`.

post.description:
Replace the current user's file storage settings. Requires the `admin` right.

**Send the settings fields at the top level of the request body**, not wrapped in a `file_storage_settings` object. The operation deserializes the whole body into the settings object, so a wrapped body is accepted, returns `success: true`, and silently writes defaults instead of the values supplied.

**This is a full replacement**: an omitted field is written as its default.

auto_overwrite.description: Whether uploading a file with an existing name overwrites it. Defaults to `false` when omitted.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right.

post.description:
Read one interface setting by key.

A key that was never written returns `value: null` with HTTP 200. It is not an error: the operation has no error path.

key.description: Setting key. 1 to 50 characters, and may contain only English letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

value.description: The stored value, or null if the key has never been written.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Write one interface setting.

Both `key` and `value` are required, and `value` may not be null. **A setting cannot be removed**, only overwritten, since no delete operation exists and null is rejected.

key.description: Setting key. 1 to 50 characters, and may contain only English letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

value.description: Value to store. 0 to 8192 characters. May not be null, though an empty string is accepted.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Over quota, error code 268.

post.description:
Change the password for the current user.

**Requires a password-change session**, so an ordinary session hash or API key cannot call this operation.

Changing a password ends every other session for the account.

password.description:
New password for the user. 12 to 20 characters, combining uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, and at least one special character. A password matching any of the last 10 used is rejected.

The API enforces this through the platform password policy, which `userGetInfo` returns as `paas_settings.password_policy`, including which characters count as special.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: In demo mode this function is disabled, error code 101.

post.description:
Set a new password for the current user.

**Requires a session hash, and a standard session specifically. An API key is rejected** with error code 4.

Setting a password ends every other session for the account.

new_password.description:
New password for the user. 12 to 20 characters, combining uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, and at least one special character. A password matching any of the last 10 used is rejected.

The API enforces this through the platform password policy, which `userGetInfo` returns as `paas_settings.password_policy`, including which characters count as special.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: In demo mode this function is disabled, error code 101. Error codes 245 new password must be different and 248 wrong password return the default 400.

post.description:
Extend the lifetime of the current session.

A session expires on an absolute deadline set when it was created, **30 days later by default**, and using the session does not push that deadline back. This operation replaces the deadline with a fresh full lifetime starting now, so a session with 2 days left and one with 29 days left both end up with the same 30 days. The period is a per-installation setting, so treat 30 days as the default rather than a constant.

An API key has no expiry and needs no renewal.

**Requires a session hash. An API key is rejected** with error code 4, "User or API key not found or session ended", which is misleading: the key is valid, but this operation accepts standard sessions only.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return the delivery session hash for the current user, used by the delivery application.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Create a delivery session for the current user.

Requires the `delivery_session_create` right.

Takes no parameters. Also accepts GET.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Feature unavailable due to tariff restrictions, error code 236.

403.description: In demo mode this function is disabled, error code 101.

post.description: Associate a push notification token with the current session, so the platform can deliver push notifications to that device.

token.description: Push token, or the endpoint from `pushSubscription` as a full URL when the application is `w3c_pushapi`.

parameters.description: Only for `w3c_pushapi`. Carries the keys from `pushSubscription`, `p256dh` and `auth`.

category_filter.description: Optional. Which notification categories to deliver. Defaults to `*`, meaning all. A comma-separated list allows only those categories; the same list prefixed with a minus allows all except those.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Remove the push notification token associated with the current session.

Takes no parameters. Returns error code 201, not found in database, when the session has no token bound.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Append a check-in record to the audit log for the current user. This **writes** an audit entry; it does not read one.

**Requires a session hash. An API key is rejected** with error code 4, "User or API key not found or session ended", which is misleading: the key is valid, but this operation accepts standard sessions only.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return audit records for the current user and their sub-users. Requires the `admin` right.

Note that a request with an empty body reports `interval` as the missing required parameter. That is the internal field name; the public parameters are `from` and `to`, and both forms work.

from.description: Include records recorded at or after this date and time.

to.description: Include records recorded at or before this date and time.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return.

actions.description: Optional. Restrict to these action names.

sort.description: Optional. Sort options, each a property and direction such as `action_date=asc`. Sortable properties are `action`, `action_date`, `action_datetime`, `user`, and `host`. Defaults to `["action_date=asc"]`.

grouping.description: Optional. How to group the log.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right.

post.description:
List the custom applications registered for the account, enabled or not.

**This operation needs no right of its own, only a valid session, and it returns the stored key of every application whose `authorization.type` is `api_key`.**

Callable with an empty body. Also accepts GET.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Register a custom application for the account.

`id` and `enabled` are accepted and ignored: a new application is always created enabled, and `user/application/enabled/set` hides it afterwards.

**`icon` is not length-checked and is stored in a 50-character column**, so a longer value fails with error code 1, a database error, rather than a validation error.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

Requires the `admin` right.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error code 268, over quota: the account already holds as many applications as the platform allows.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right.

post.description:
Replace an existing application.

**This is a full replacement, not a merge.** Every optional field left out is reset to its default: `enabled` to `true`, `authorization` to `user_session`, `display_method` to `new_tab`, `icon` to `extension`, and `description` to empty. Send the whole object, not only the fields being changed.

**The length limits are not enforced here, unlike on create.** An over-long `label`, `url_template`, `description`, or `icon` fails with error code 1, a database error, instead of error code 7. Types and enum values are still checked and still give error code 7.

`id` has to name an existing application of this account. Naming one that does not exist, or leaving `id` out, returns error code 201, not found in database.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

Requires the `admin` right.

application.description: The replacement application, identified by its `id`.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right.

post.description:
Delete an application. It leaves the side menu immediately.

Returns error code 201, not found in database, when no application of this account carries that identifier. **Leaving `application_id` out returns 201 as well, rather than a validation error.**

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

Requires the `admin` right.

application_id.description: Identifier of the application to delete.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right.

post.summary: Show or hide a user application
post.description:
Show or hide an application in the side menu, leaving everything else about it unchanged.

**`enabled` is not treated as missing when it is left out: it falls back to `false` and the application is hidden.** Always send it.

Returns error code 201, not found in database, when no application of this account carries that identifier. Leaving `application_id` out returns 201 as well.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

Requires the `admin` right.

application_id.description: Identifier of the application to show or hide.

enabled.description: Whether the application appears in the side menu. Falls back to `false` when left out, which hides it.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Operation not permitted, error code 13: the caller lacks the `admin` right.

post.description:
Create a vehicle. Pass a vehicle object without its `id`.

Requires the `vehicle_update` right.

vehicle.description: The vehicle to create, without the `id` field.

force_reassign.description: Optional. Default `true`. Reassign the device to this vehicle even if it was assigned to another one.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

409.description: Error 247: a device cannot be assigned, or a uniqueness constraint failed.

post.description:
Delete vehicles by ID.

**Exactly one of `vehicle_id` or `vehicle_ids` must be given.** A request with neither reports a missing parameter named `has_at_least_one_vehicle_id`, which is the internal name of the validation group enforcing that choice, not a parameter you can send.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

Requires the `vehicle_update` right.

vehicle_id.description: ID of a single vehicle to delete. Use this or `vehicle_ids`, not both.

vehicle_ids.description: IDs of vehicles to delete. Use this or `vehicle_id`, not both.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
List the vehicles of the current user, with pagination, sorting and a text filter.

Callable with an empty body. Also accepts GET.

limit.description: Pagination. Maximum number of vehicle records to return.

offset.description: Pagination. Return vehicles starting from this offset.

sort.description: Optional. Sort options, each a property and direction such as `type=desc`. **At most 2 options per request.** Sortable properties: `id`, `label`, `reg_number`, `model`, `type`, `garage_organization_name`, `vin`, `tracker_label`, `fuel_type`, `fuel_grade`, `norm_avg_fuel_consumption`, `fuel_tank_volume`, `payload_weight`, `chassis_number`, `subtype`, `wheel_arrangement`, `tyres_number`, `tyres_size`, `max_speed`, `passengers`.

filter.description: Optional. Filter by VIN, reg_number or label. Up to 100 characters, or null.

count.description: Total number of vehicles matching the request, ignoring pagination.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return one vehicle by ID.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Update a vehicle. Pass a full vehicle object including its `id`.

Note `icon_id` cannot be set here: it is changed through `vehicle/avatar/assign`.

Requires the `vehicle_update` right.

vehicle.description: The vehicle to update, including its `id`.

force_reassign.description: Optional. Default `true`. Reassign the device to this vehicle even if it was assigned to another one.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

409.description: Error 247: a device cannot be assigned. Error 261: the vehicle is referenced by something that prevents the change.

post.description:
Parse a tab-delimited batch of vehicles and return them checked, with per-row errors. Does not create anything.

Give either `batch` or `file_id`. **If `file_id` is set, `batch` is ignored.** A request with neither returns error 7 with no `errors` array, because the rule is cross-field rather than per-parameter.

Requires the `vehicle_update` right.

file_id.description: Preloaded file ID. Takes precedence over `batch`.

fields.description: Optional. Field names, in column order. Defaults to `["label", "model", "reg_number", "fuel_grade"]`.

limit_exceeded.description: `true` if the given batch was constrained by a limit.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 234: the file or batch exceeds a size limit.

post.description:
Assign an icon to a vehicle.

Set `icon_id` to null to use an uploaded avatar instead of an icon.

**`icon_color` is required** as well as `vehicle_id`.

Create an API key, and return it.

An API key is the same thing as a session hash but with unlimited lifetime. It survives a logout and a password change, needs no renewal, does not require storing a login and password, can be revoked on its own, and has a separate rate-limit counter from ordinary user requests.

**Up to 20 keys per account.** Give each one a meaningful title so they can be told apart.

**A standard session hash is required, and an API key is rejected** with error 4, "User or API key not found or session ended", which is misleading because the key itself is valid. Get a session hash from `user/auth`. **Master users only**, since the operation needs the `admin` right.

The required right depends on the entity type: `place` needs `places_custom_fields_update`, and other types need the right their own product defines.

Which report is produced is decided by `plugin.plugin_id`, and most of the `plugin` object is plugin-specific. See the tracker report plugins reference for what each one accepts.

Report by trackers takes `trackers`; a report by employees takes `employees` instead.

**Error 211 carries extra data.** When the period is too long the error body includes `max_time_span`, a human-readable English string such as `120 days` rather than an ISO 8601 duration, so a caller can retry with a period that fits rather than guessing.

post.description:
Return the tracks of an asset over a period, one entry per tracker the asset was attached to.

Each entry carries its own `interval`, which is the window during which the asset was attached to that tracker, not the window you asked for.

This is the **asset** track resource, `asset/track/*`, which takes an asset and resolves its trackers for you. It is a different resource from `track/*`, which takes tracker IDs directly.

A request with an empty body reports `interval` as a missing parameter alongside `asset`. That is the internal name of the field holding both dates; the public parameters are `from` and `to`.

asset.description: Which asset to report on. The tracker list is derived from the trackers currently related to this asset.

type.description: What kind of asset it is.

from.description: Start of the period. The response begins with the next track point after this time.

to.description: End of the period. Must be later than `from`.

filter.description: Optional. Default `true`. Drop tracks judged too short by length and point count.

split.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false`, all tracks in the period are combined into one, returned as a `merged` track.

include_gsm_lbs.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false`, GSM LBS points are excluded.

cluster_single_reports.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, single-point trips are grouped by coordinates into `cluster` tracks.

count_events.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, each multi-point track carries `event_count`.

omit_addresses.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, address fields come back empty.

with_points.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, each track carries its `points_list`.

point_limit.description: Optional. Reduce the returned points to about this many, from 2 to 3000. Without it the server's own simplification settings apply. **Not a hard limit**: the response may contain more.

tracker_id.description: Tracker identifier.

limit_exceeded.description: `true` when the requested period is longer than the tracker's plan stores, so the data is truncated.

interval.description: When the asset was attached to this tracker, which is not necessarily the period requested.

from.description: Start of the attachment interval.

to.description: End of the attachment interval.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

This is the **asset** track resource, `asset/track/*`, which takes an asset and resolves its trackers for you. It is a different resource from `track/*`, which takes tracker IDs directly.

A request with an empty body reports `interval` as a missing parameter alongside `asset`. That is the internal name of the field holding both dates; the public parameters are `from` and `to`.

asset.description: Which asset to report on. The tracker list is derived from the trackers currently related to this asset.

type.description: What kind of asset it is.

to.description: End of the period. Must be later than `from`.

track_id.description: Optional. Return only the points of this track. Without it, every valid track point in the period is returned.

include_gsm_lbs.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false` **and no `track_id` is given**, GSM LBS points are excluded.

simplify.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `true`, the returned data is simplified to fewer points.

point_limit.description: Optional. Only applies when `simplify` is `true`. Reduce the returned points to about this many, from 2 to 3000. **Not a hard limit**: the response may contain more.

filter.description: Optional. When `true`, tracks are filtered, which currently affects LBS tracks only. When `false`, parking points are included.

200.description: The asset's track points, per tracker

tracker_id.description: Tracker identifier.

limit_exceeded.description: `true` when the requested period is longer than the tracker's plan stores.

interval.description: When the asset was attached to this tracker.

from.description: Start of the attachment interval.

to.description: End of the attachment interval.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Error 211: the period between `from` and `to` is longer than the API configuration allows.

**A coordinate pair in `q` is handled as reverse geocoding instead.** When `q` is two decimal numbers separated by a comma, such as `37.825014,-122.372020`, it is read as latitude and longitude and the address at that point is returned as a single result. Requires the `statuses` tariff feature on at least one tracker. Without it the call returns error 236.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

post.description:
Create a geo link, a shareable session that shows the live location of chosen trackers to someone without an account. Returns the new link's ID.

A new link is **active as soon as it is created**: its `enabled` flag comes back `true` and the URL works immediately, so treat the returned hash as live from that moment. Deactivate it with `tracker/location/link/status/change`.

An account can hold up to 10,000 geo links.

The geo link object is **flattened into the request body**: its fields are sent at the top level rather than nested under an object. `hash`, `create_date`, `creator_id`, `user_id` and `enabled` are read-only. Sending them is accepted and ignored rather than refused, so it changes nothing. Do not send `hash`: it collides with the legacy `hash` authentication parameter and the request fails with error 3.

Requires the `weblocator_session_create` right, which additionally needs the `weblocator` tariff feature on at least one tracker.

description.description: Description of the link. At most 255 printable characters; may be empty but must be present.

trackers.description: The trackers the link shows, and what it shows of each. 1 to 100 entries.

value.description: ID of the new geo link.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: at least one of the trackers lacks the `weblocator` tariff feature. Error 268: the account's quota for geo links is exhausted.

403.description: Error 13: the caller lacks the required right. Error 217: one or more of the tracker IDs does not exist or belongs to another user.

404.description: Error 204: one or more of the geofences, places or place custom fields was not found.

post.description:
Replace a geo link's description, lifetime, trackers and parameters. **`id` is required**, and everything else is replaced by what is sent rather than merged.

The trackers, geofences, places and custom fields are re-checked only where the list actually changed, so an update that leaves them alone will not fail on an entity that has since become inaccessible.

Sending them is accepted and ignored rather than refused, so it changes nothing. Do not send `hash`: it collides with the legacy `hash` authentication parameter and the request fails with error 3.

Requires the `weblocator_session_create` right, which additionally needs the `weblocator` tariff feature on at least one tracker.

description.description: Description of the link. At most 255 printable characters; may be empty but must be present.

post.description:
Turn a geo link on or off without deleting it. Deactivating one also closes any sessions currently open against it.

**`is_active` defaults to `false`**, so a call that passes only `id` deactivates the link. Send it explicitly.

The change is recorded in the audit log. Setting the status it already has succeeds and does nothing.

Requires the `weblocator_session_create` right, which additionally needs the `weblocator` tariff feature on at least one tracker.

is_active.description: Default `false`. `true` activates the link, `false` deactivates it.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return one geo link by ID, including its `hash`, which is what identifies the link to the person it was shared with.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return the account's geo links, with filtering, search conditions, sorting and pagination.

`filter` and `conditions` may be combined, in which case a link must match both.

Callable with an empty body. Also accepts GET.

filter.description: Optional. Free-text filter applied across the searchable fields. At most 100 printable characters.

conditions.description: Optional. Search conditions. The fields available are `trackers` (labels of all trackers on the link), `aliases`, `description`, and `creator` (the creator's full name, master user only).

offset.description: Optional. Default 0. Offset into the results, for pagination.

limit.description: Optional. Default and maximum 10000.

sort.description: Optional. Default `["id=asc"]`. Each entry pairs a field with a direction, for example `"create_date=desc"`. At most 8 entries, no duplicates. The fields available are `id`, `create_date`, `expire_date`, `status`, `trackers`, `aliases`, `description`, and `creator` (master user only). Directions are `asc` and `desc`; an entry without a direction is rejected. Sorting by `status` orders enabled, then not yet started, then expired, then disabled.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Delete a geo link. Anyone holding the link loses access immediately.

Unlike creating, updating and switching a link, deleting one needs no specific right.

post.description:
Create an empty working status list. Statuses are added to it afterwards with `status/create`.

Pass the listing object without `id` and without `entries`: both are rejected on creation, since a new list has no statuses in it yet.

Requires the `tracker_update` right. Requires the `statuses` tariff feature on at least one tracker. Without it the call returns error 236.

listing.description: The status list to create, without `id` and without `entries`.

id.description: ID of the new working status list.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: no tracker on the account has the `statuses` feature. Error 268: the account's quota for working status lists is exhausted.

post.description:
Delete a working status list and everything in it.

Requires the `tracker_update` right. Requires the `statuses` tariff feature on at least one tracker. Without it the call returns error 236.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

listing_id.description: ID of the working status list.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: no tracker on the account has the `statuses` feature.

post.description:
Return every working status list belonging to the account, each with its `entries` in display order.

Callable with an empty body. Requires the `statuses` tariff feature on at least one tracker. Without it the call returns error 236.

Also accepts GET.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: no tracker on the account has the `statuses` feature.

post.description:
Update a working status list's label, control flags and status order.

**`entries` must contain exactly the statuses already in the list**, no more and no fewer, with no duplicates. It exists to set their display order, not to add or remove statuses; a mismatched set returns error 262. Use `status/create` and `status/delete` to change membership.

Updating the list invalidates the status cache on every tracker assigned to it.

Requires the `tracker_update` right. Requires the `statuses` tariff feature on at least one tracker. Without it the call returns error 236.

listing.description: The status list to update, including `id` and the full `entries` array.

post.summary: Assign working status list to tracker
post.description:
Assign a working status list to a tracker, or remove the assignment.

**Omit `listing_id` entirely to remove the assignment.** A tracker with no list assigned has no working statuses available to it.

Not allowed for clones. Requires the `tracker_update` right. Requires the `statuses` tariff feature on at least one tracker. Without it the call returns error 236.

Also accepts GET with the same parameters as query-string values.

tracker_id.description: ID of the tracker, also known as the object ID. Must belong to the current account and not be blocked.

listing_id.description: Optional. ID of the working status list to assign. **Omit to remove the current assignment.**

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: no tracker on the account has the `statuses` feature.

403.description: Error 208: the tracker exists but is blocked, normally because its tariff ended. Error 219: the tracker is a clone.

post.description:
Return a driving route from `start` to `end`, through any `waypoints`, using a routing provider.

**Omit `provider_type` to use the account's configured default provider.** The three provider-specific paths are the same operation with the provider pinned.

Requires the `routing` tariff feature on **every** tracker on the account. Without it the call returns error 236.

waypoints.description: Optional. Intermediate points, visited in the order given unless the provider reorders them. **At most 98**, since start and end count towards the provider's hundred-point limit.

point_limit.description: Optional. Simplify the returned route to at most this many points.

provider_type.description: Optional. Routing provider to use. Omit to use the account's configured default.

minsize.description: Optional. Default 5. Smoothing threshold in metres. Setting it below the distance between two neighbouring pixels at the current zoom is not recommended.

use_traffic.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `false` the router runs in `optimal` mode ignoring traffic; when `true` it runs in `comfort` mode using it.

list.description: The route as an ordered list of points.

key_points.description: The start, each waypoint and the end, in that order, located within `list`. Each entry carries the cumulative `distance` and `time` from the start.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: at least one tracker on the account lacks the `routing` tariff feature.

403.description: Error 215: the routing provider returned an error. Error 218: the routing provider rejected the parameters, most often because a point could not be matched to a road or no route exists between them. Both carry an `errors` array in the response body describing what the provider said.

post.description:
Return a route calculated by the Google Directions API. Identical to `route/get` with `provider_type` pinned to `google`; a `provider_type` sent here is ignored.

Google allows at most 8 waypoints besides the origin and destination, or 23 for Maps API for Business customers. Exceeding that is reported as error 218 with `MAX_WAYPOINTS_EXCEEDED`.

Requires the `routing` tariff feature on **every** tracker on the account. Without it the call returns error 236.

waypoints.description: Optional. Intermediate points, visited in the order given unless the provider reorders them. **At most 98**, since start and end count towards the provider's hundred-point limit.

point_limit.description: Optional. Simplify the returned route to at most this many points.

list.description: The route as an ordered list of points.

key_points.description: The start, each waypoint and the end, in that order, located within `list`. Each entry carries the cumulative `distance` and `time` from the start, both 0 for the start point itself.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: at least one tracker on the account lacks the `routing` tariff feature.

403.description: Error 215: the Google service failed. The `errors` array holds one of `OVER_QUERY_LIMIT`, `REQUEST_DENIED` or `UNKNOWN_ERROR`. Error 218: Google rejected the parameters. The `errors` array holds one of `NOT_FOUND`, `ZERO_RESULTS`, `MAX_WAYPOINTS_EXCEEDED` or `INVALID_REQUEST`.

post.description:
Return a route calculated by OSRM. Identical to `route/get` with `provider_type` pinned to `osrm`; a `provider_type` sent here is ignored.

Requires the `routing` tariff feature on **every** tracker on the account. Without it the call returns error 236.

waypoints.description: Optional. Intermediate points, visited in the order given unless the provider reorders them. **At most 98**, since start and end count towards the provider's hundred-point limit.

point_limit.description: Optional. Simplify the returned route to at most this many points.

list.description: The route as an ordered list of points.

key_points.description: The start, each waypoint and the end, in that order, located within `list`. Each entry carries the cumulative `distance` and `time` from the start.

The `errors` array holds objects with `status`, either `NOT_FOUND` when a point could not be matched or no route exists, or `UNKNOWN_ERROR`; plus `status_code` and `message` passed through from OSRM, neither of which should be relied on.

post.description:
Return a route calculated by the Progorod router. Identical to `route/get` with `provider_type` pinned to `progorod`; a `provider_type` sent here is ignored.

**Progorod may reorder the waypoints.** It is also the only provider that reads `minsize` and `use_traffic`; the other three accept them and ignore them.

Requires the `routing` tariff feature on **every** tracker on the account. Without it the call returns error 236.

waypoints.description: Optional. Intermediate points, visited in the order given unless the provider reorders them. **At most 98**, since start and end count towards the provider's hundred-point limit.

point_limit.description: Optional. Simplify the returned route to at most this many points.

minsize.description: Optional. Default 5. Smoothing threshold in metres. Setting it below the distance between two neighbouring pixels at the current zoom is not recommended.

use_traffic.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `false` the router runs in `optimal` mode ignoring traffic; when `true` it runs in `comfort` mode using it.

list.description: The route as an ordered list of points.

key_points.description: The start, each waypoint and the end, in that order, located within `list`. Each entry carries the cumulative `distance` and `time` from the start.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

402.description: Error 236: at least one tracker on the account lacks the `routing` tariff feature.

403.description: Error 215: the Progorod service failed. Error 218: Progorod rejected the parameters. The `errors` array holds objects with `type`, one of `not_set`, `malformed` or `isolated`; `point`, one of `start`, `end`, `waypoint` or `all`; and `index`, the position in `waypoints`, present only when `point` is `waypoint`.

post.description:
Return the tracker's tracks over a period, with totals across all of them.

What comes back depends on three switches. `split` decides whether the period is broken into separate trips or returned as one `merged` track. `cluster_single_reports` groups one-point trips by coordinate into `cluster` tracks. `filter` drops tracks judged too short by length and point count.

Points are left out unless `with_points` is set.

tracker_id.description: ID of the tracker, also known as the object ID. Must belong to the current account and not be blocked.

from.description: Start of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format, in the account's timezone.

to.description: End of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format. Must be after `from`.

filter.description: Optional. Default `true`. Drop tracks that are too short by length and number of points.

split.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false`, the whole period is returned as a single `merged` track.

include_gsm_lbs.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false`, GSM LBS points are excluded.

cluster_single_reports.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, one-point trips are grouped by coordinate into `cluster` tracks.

count_events.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, each track that is not a single point carries `event_count`.

omit_addresses.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, the address fields come back empty, which is faster.

point_limit.description: Optional. Reduce the result to about this many points. Not a hard limit: the result can hold slightly more. Omit to use the platform's own simplification settings.

list.description: Zero or more tracks. Empty means there were no trips matching the options, or the device sent no points.

limit_exceeded.description: `true` when the requested period reaches further back than the tracker's plan allows. The period is silently clipped rather than refused, so a `true` here means the result covers less than was asked for.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Error 208: the tracker exists but is blocked, normally because its tariff ended. Error 211: the period between `from` and `to` exceeds the maximum the platform allows. Unlike the same code on `track/visit/list`, this one carries no `max_time_span`.

post.description:
Return the individual points a tracker recorded over a period, or the points of one track.

Each point's timestamp is when the tracker recorded it, converted to the account's timezone.

Reachable from a geo-link session as well as an ordinary one.

tracker_id.description: ID of the tracker, also known as the object ID. Must belong to the current account and not be blocked.

from.description: Start of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format, in the account's timezone.

to.description: End of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format. Must be after `from`.

track_id.description: Optional. Return only the points of this track. Omit to return every valid point in the period.

include_gsm_lbs.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false` **and no `track_id` is given**, GSM LBS points are excluded.

simplify.description: Optional. Default `true`. Reduce the number of points returned.

point_limit.description: Optional. Reduce the result to about this many points. Not a hard limit: the result can hold slightly more. Omit to use the platform's own simplification settings.

filter.description: Optional. Default `true`. Filter the points, which currently affects LBS tracks only. Setting it to `false` also brings parking points into the result.

limit_exceeded.description: `true` when the requested period reaches further back than the tracker's plan allows. The period is silently clipped rather than refused, so a `true` here means the result covers less than was asked for.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Error 208: the tracker exists but is blocked, normally because its tariff ended. Error 211: the period between `from` and `to` exceeds the maximum the platform allows. Unlike the same code on `track/visit/list`, this one carries no `max_time_span`.

post.description:
Return the tracker's points over a period as a KML or KMZ file, for opening in another mapping application.

**The response is the file itself**, not a JSON envelope. The one exception is when the tracker's plan does not reach back far enough to cover any of the requested period, in which case a JSON body comes back with `limit_exceeded` set and an empty `list`.

tracker_id.description: ID of the tracker, also known as the object ID. Must belong to the current account and not be blocked.

from.description: Start of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format, in the account's timezone.

to.description: End of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format. Must be after `from`.

track_ids.description: Optional. Include only these tracks. Omit to include every valid point in the period. No duplicates.

include_gsm_lbs.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false` **and no `track_ids` are given**, GSM LBS points are excluded.

simplify.description: Optional. Default `true`. Reduce the number of points in the file.

point_limit.description: Optional. Reduce the result to about this many points. Not a hard limit: the result can hold slightly more. Omit to use the platform's own simplification settings.

filter.description: Optional. Default `true`. Filter the points, which currently affects LBS tracks only.

split.description: Optional. Default `false`. When `true`, the file groups tracks into folders split by stops, each with start and end markers.

200.description: The track as a KML or KMZ file

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Error 208: the tracker exists but is blocked, normally because its tariff ended. Error 211: the period between `from` and `to` exceeds the maximum the platform allows. Unlike the same code on `track/visit/list`, this one carries no `max_time_span`.

post.description:
Return the IDs of the geofences and places that contain at least one of the tracker's points in the period.

Both lists come back empty when the account has no geofences and no places, and each is empty when its `include_` switch is `false`.

**This call has its own period limit**, separate from the one the other track calls use, and it is usually shorter.

tracker_id.description: ID of the tracker, also known as the object ID. Must belong to the current account and not be blocked.

from.description: Start of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format, in the account's timezone.

to.description: End of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format. Must be after `from`.

include_zones.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false`, `zones` comes back empty.

include_places.description: Optional. Default `true`. When `false`, `places` comes back empty.

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

403.description: Error 208: the tracker exists but is blocked, normally because its tariff ended. Error 211: the period exceeds this call's own maximum, which is much shorter than the one the other track calls use. The response body carries `max_time_span`, **a human-readable English string such as `26 hours`, not an ISO 8601 duration**.

404.description: Error 204: no tracker with this ID belongs to the current account.

post.description:
Build a waybill for the tracker's tracks over a period and return it as a DOCX file.

**This call has a side effect**: it stores the waybill number, which `track/waybill/settings/read` then returns. A number consisting only of digits is incremented before being stored, so the next waybill can carry on the sequence.

Its track defaults differ from `track/list`: `include_gsm_lbs` defaults to `false` and `cluster_single_reports` to `true`, because that produces a cleaner document.

tracker_id.description: ID of the tracker, also known as the object ID. Must belong to the current account and not be blocked.

from.description: Start of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format, in the account's timezone.

to.description: End of the period, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format. Must be after `from`.

number.description: Waybill number. 1 to 10 characters from letters, digits, spaces and `- _ № # ? %`.

series.description: Optional. Waybill series. Same 1 to 10 character rule as `number`.

type.description: Optional. Default `form3`. Which waybill form to produce. `form3` is the passenger-car form 3, `form3ext` its extended variant for longer periods, and `form4c` and `form4cext` the freight forms.

fill_odometer.description: Optional. When `true`, mileage readings are written into the document's odometer fields.

filter.description: Optional. Default `true`. Drop tracks that are too short by length and number of points.

include_gsm_lbs.description: Optional. **Default `false` here**, unlike `track/list`. When `true`, GSM LBS tracks are included.

cluster_single_reports.description: Optional. **Default `true` here**, unlike `track/list`. When `false`, one-point trips are not grouped by coordinate.

200.description: The waybill as a DOCX file

400.description: Bad request. The response body carries the API-level error code in `status.code`. Validation failures also include an `errors` array naming each offending parameter.

post.description:
Return the waybill number stored by the last `track/waybill/download` call, already incremented if it was all digits.

Returns error 201 when the account has never downloaded a waybill.

Callable with an empty body. Also accepts GET.

post.description:
Get every integrated tracker model. Available to demo accounts.

The list is large, around 1,800 models, so use `codes` when you already know which ones you want.

compact_view.description: Optional. Default `false`. Return a reduced view of each model.

compact_index.description: Optional. Default `false`, and **deprecated**. Compact the indexed inputs, returning only the input with the highest index.

codes.description: Optional. Model codes. When given, only those models are returned.

post.description: Get the current state of one tracker: GPS, GSM, inputs, outputs, battery and movement. Reachable from a geo link or delivery session as well as a normal one.

post.summary: Read the state of several trackers
post.description:
Get current state for many trackers at once. Reachable from a geo link session as well as a normal one.

`trackers` is optional: **omitting it returns every tracker on the account**. At most 2,000 per request, so split larger fleets across calls.

By default a single blocked or missing tracker fails the whole call. `list_blocked` and `allow_not_exist` turn those into `blocked` and `not_exist` arrays alongside the results, which is almost always what a fleet-wide caller wants.

list_blocked.description: Optional. Default `false`. Return blocked tracker IDs in `blocked` instead of failing with error 208.

allow_not_exist.description: Optional. Default `false`. Return unknown tracker IDs in `not_exist` instead of failing with error 217 or 201.

post.description:
Register a new device and link it to the current account, configuring it to send data to the platform where the model supports that. The panel must have an SMS gateway installed.

**Registration plugins matter.** Each plugin has its own extra parameters, and you must send those alongside the ones below. `commons/plugin` lists them. A Queclink registered through plugin 37, for example, also needs `phone`, `apn_name`, `apn_user`, `apn_password` and `activation_code`.

`device_id` is validated in two stages, both returning error 7. First a general character and length check, reported as `must match "^[0-9a-zA-Z\-]{1,64}$"`, which rejects underscores, spaces, punctuation and non-latin characters. Then the length range the model's `id_type` requires. **Read the range from the error message rather than from the model metadata**, which can be wider: models declaring `ascii,6,64` reject anything over 32 characters.

Requires the `tracker_register` right.

api_key.description: Either a user session hash or an API key, with the "NVX " prefix, for example "NVX 22eac1c27af4be7b9d04da2ce1af111b". Obtain a session hash from the userAuth operation, or create an API key from the API keys operations. A small number of operations accept a session hash only and reject an API key with error code 4; each says so in its description.
api_key.name: Authorization

status.description: Error status. Present only when an error occurred.

code.description: An error code in this API, not an HTTP code.

description.description: An error description.

errors.description: Per-parameter detail, returned with validation failures such as error code 7. A parameter name here may be an internal field name rather than the documented parameter name.

parameter.description: Name of the parameter that failed validation.

UserSettings.description: A user's locale, display, and provider preferences. Filtered by the dealer's GIS package before being returned, so a field may be absent on a restricted package.

date_format.description: Optional. Date representation: `ddMMyyyy_dots` is 01.12.2021, `ddMMyyyy_slashes` is 01/12/2021, `MMddyyyy_hyphens` is 12-01-2021, `yyyyMMdd_hyphens` is 2021-12-01, `dMMMy` is 1 Dec 2021, `dMMMMy` is 1 December 2021.

hour_mode.description: Optional. Time representation: `TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS` is a 24-hour clock such as 17:45, `TWELVE_HOURS` is a 12-hour clock such as 5:45 PM.

auto_overwrite.description: Whether uploading a file with an existing name overwrites it.

emails.description: Email addresses that receive balance alerts.

TariffRestrictions.description: Limits imposed by the user's tariff.

UserInfo.description: The current user. Address and legal fields are present but empty when never set.

login.description: User's login, usually an email address.

balance.description: Current account balance. A decimal, returned with four fractional digits.

bonus.description: Current bonus balance. A decimal, returned with four fractional digits.

demo.description: Whether this is a demo account.

verified.description: Whether the account email is verified.

phone_verified.description: Whether the account phone is verified.

default_security_group_id.description: Identifier of the security group new sub-users join by default.

iec.description: Industrial Enterprises Classifier, also known as KPP. Used in Russia.

registered_region.description: Region part of the registered address.

registered_index.description: Index part of the registered address.

registered_city.description: City part of the registered address.

registered_street_address.description: Street part of the registered address.

gis_package.description: Active GIS package, which determines which user settings fields are returned.

password_policy.description: Rules a new password must satisfy.

title.description: Preset title, or a localisation key such as `menu-editor.default-preset`.

UserApplication.description:
A custom application embedded into the platform interface and reachable from the side menu.

**One `authorization` object, three shapes, selected by `type`.** `none` opens the URL with no credential, `user_session` passes the current platform session, and `api_key` passes a fixed key and is the only shape that carries `hash`.

id.description: Application identifier. Absent when creating, required when updating.

label.description: Name shown in the side menu. Not blank, 1 to 50 characters, trimmed before it is stored.

url_template.description: URL the application opens at. May carry placeholders that the interface substitutes when a user opens it: `{locale_code}`, `{user_identifier}`, and `{timezone}`. 4 to 1000 characters, trimmed before it is stored.

enabled.description: Whether the application appears in the side menu. Ignored on create, where a new application is always enabled. Defaults to `true` on update.

authorization.description: How the application is authorised when its URL is opened. Defaults to `user_session`.

type.description: Which of the three shapes this is, and therefore whether `hash` applies.

hash.description: The API key to pass. **`api_key` only, and required for it.**

display_method.description: How the application opens: `new_tab` in a new browser tab, `embedded` inside the platform interface. Defaults to `new_tab`.

icon.description: Icon name shown beside the label in the side menu, for example `dashboard` or `camera`. Defaults to `extension`. Not checked against a list of names, and **not length-checked either, while the column holds 50 characters**.

description.description: Longer plain-text description shown to users. Up to 1000 characters, trimmed before it is stored. Defaults to empty.

AuditLogRecord.description: One audit log entry. Fields that do not apply to the recorded action are absent.

user_id.description: Master user the record belongs to.

entry_category.description: Category of the entity acted on, for example `user` or `custom_field`.

entry_id.description: Identifier of the entity acted on, when the action targets one.

payload.description: Additional information about the action. Typically the fields that changed. Absent or null for actions that carry none.

host.description: Source IP address of the request, IPv4 or IPv6.

user_agent.description: User agent of the client that made the request.

icon_color.description: Colour of the vehicle icon, as six hex digits without a leading `#`.

status_id.description: ID of the vehicle status currently assigned, or null when none is. Set it with `vehicle/status/*`.

trailer_reg_number.description: Registration number of the attached trailer. Empty string when there is none.

type.description: Vehicle's type.

subtype.description: Optional. Depends on `type`; null means undefined. For `car`: sedan, universal, hatchback, liftback, limousine, pickup, minivan, coupe, coupe4d, muscle, convertible, phaeton, lando, crossover, roadster, suv. For `truck`: tipper, board, covered, awning, mixer, tanker, refrigerator, transporter, container, tractor. For `bus`: city, shuttle, platform, school, intercity, sightseeing. For `special`: mobile_crane, racing, buggy, ambulance, firefighter, hearse, shop, harvester, snowplow, tractor, grader, excavator, bulldozer, armored, amphibian, boat.

color.description: Optional. Colour of the vehicle, as free text rather than RGB.

norm_avg_fuel_consumption.description: Normal average fuel consumption, litres per 100 km.

fuel_cost.description: Optional. Cost of fuel per litre.

liability_insurance_valid_till.description: Date the liability insurance is valid until.

free_insurance_valid_till.description: Date the free insurance is valid until.

icon_id.description: ID of the icon. **Read-only here**: change it through `vehicleAvatarAssign`.

avatar_file_name.description: File name of the uploaded avatar.

tags.description: IDs of tags applied to the vehicle.

CheckedVehicle.description: A vehicle parsed from a batch, with the same fields as a vehicle plus any per-row problems found while checking it.

For `truck`: tipper, board, covered, awning, mixer, tanker, refrigerator, transporter, container, tractor. For `bus`: city, shuttle, platform, school, intercity, sightseeing. For `special`: mobile_crane, racing, buggy, ambulance, firefighter, hearse, shop, harvester, snowplow, tractor, grader, excavator, bulldozer, armored, amphibian, boat.

color.description: Optional. Colour of the vehicle, as free text rather than RGB.

norm_avg_fuel_consumption.description: Normal average fuel consumption, litres per 100 km.

fuel_cost.description: Optional. Cost of fuel per litre.

liability_insurance_valid_till.description: Date the liability insurance is valid until.

free_insurance_valid_till.description: Date the free insurance is valid until.
